title: Rethinking Evidence Hierarchies in Medical Language Benchmarks: A Critical Evaluation of HealthBench

bias_targets.methodology: Analyzing the dataset composition for the representation of diseases (e.g., Neglected Tropical Diseases vs. HIV) to demonstrate a Western-centric focus, and comparing benchmark evaluation rubrics against diverse regional clinical guidelines (e.g., US/UK vs. Kenyan immunization schedules).

Critiquing the benchmark's rubric authorship process, specifically analyzing the heavy reliance on single-authored criteria (87%), to demonstrate how individual cognitive biases and localized practice variations override higher-tier evidence from Clinical Practice Guidelines (CPGs).

Evaluating the benchmark's failure to account for real-world resource constraints typical in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), such as medicine stock-outs, and proposing a contextual override logic to mitigate penalties for resource-driven care deviations.
